subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Should iOS remote Tailscale pairing stay `wss://`/Serve-only by default, or should OpenClaw add an explicit direct-CGNAT plaintext or trust-on-first-use exception for `100.64.0.0/10` Gateways?
rationale: The current code intentionally keeps raw Tailnet CGNAT and `.ts.net` plaintext fail-closed, while the reported supported secure path still fails for a real user; changing either side is a security/product boundary decision rather than a narrow mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep secure remote pairing and fix proof
options.body: Preserve `wss://`/Serve as the supported iOS Tailscale path, improve TLS/Serve diagnostics and trust prompts, and require real iPhone proof before closing.

options.title: Add explicit CGNAT exception
options.body: Permit a clearly labeled, operator-approved plaintext or TOFU direct-CGNAT mode with tests and docs explaining the security tradeoff.

options.title: Serve-only documentation path
options.body: Declare raw direct-CGNAT unsupported for first-time iOS pairing and make the app/docs steer users to Tailscale Serve or another real TLS endpoint.

recommendation.title: Keep secure remote pairing and fix proof
recommendation.body: Preserve `wss://`/Serve as the supported iOS Tailscale path, improve TLS/Serve diagnostics and trust prompts, and require real iPhone proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the most recent merged Tailscale route advertisement work and is best positioned to choose whether the remaining path is a secure-route fix or a product policy change.
